\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{उपद्रव} (upadrav)}{उपद्रव (upadrav)}]{\hi{उपद्रव} (upadrav) — a disturbance; rioting}

\label{lesson:HI-C316-upadrav}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for information, then the Hindi for to put off.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{उपद्रव}}
\textbf{\hi{उपद्रव}} — \emph{upadrav} — \textquotedblleft{}a disturbance; rioting\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{अफ़वाह} \hi{के} \hi{बाद} \hi{शहर} \hi{में} \hi{उपद्रव} \hi{हुआ।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{afvāh ke bād śahar meṁ upadrav huā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
After the rumour there was rioting in the city.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{उपद्रव}} (\emph{upadrav}) is Sanskrit \emph{upadrava}, \textquotedblleft{}what attacks or happens suddenly\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams). In the news it is unrest in the streets.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{upadrav}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{upadrav}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{afvāh ke bād śahar meṁ upadrav huā.} — After the rumour there was rioting in the city.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for information, then the Hindi for to put off, then say \emph{upadrav} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{उपद्रव} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A disturbance; rioting\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{फ़साद} (fasād)}{फ़साद (fasād)}]{\hi{फ़साद} (fasād) — trouble; strife}

\label{lesson:HI-C316-fasad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for to put off, then the Hindi for a disturbance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{फ़साद}}
\textbf{\hi{फ़साद}} — \emph{fasād} — \textquotedblleft{}trouble; strife\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{कुछ} \hi{लोग} \hi{फ़साद} \hi{करना} \hi{चाहते} \hi{थे।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kuch log fasād karnā cāhte the.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Some people wanted to make trouble.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{फ़साद}} (\emph{fasād}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{fasād}, \textquotedblleft{}disorder, a spoiling\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\hi{फ़साद} \hi{करना}} is to stir up trouble.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fasād}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{fasād}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kuch log fasād karnā cāhte the.} — Some people wanted to make trouble.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for to put off, then the Hindi for a disturbance, then say \emph{fasād} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{फूटना} (phūṭnā)}{फूटना (phūṭnā)}]{\hi{फूटना} (phūṭnā) — to burst; to shatter}

\label{lesson:HI-C316-phutna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a disturbance, then the Hindi for trouble.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{फूटना}}
\textbf{\hi{फूटना}} — \emph{phūṭnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to burst; to shatter\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{पत्थर} \hi{लगने} \hi{से} \hi{बस} \hi{का} \hi{शीशा} \hi{फूट} \hi{गया।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{patthar lagne se bas kā śīśā phūṭ gayā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A stone hit the bus and its glass shattered.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \hi{वह} \hi{बोतल} \hi{फूट} \hi{गई}, \emph{vah botal phūṭ gaī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{फूटना}} (\emph{phūṭnā}) is inherited from \emph{*sphuṭyati}, \textquotedblleft{}bursts open\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs (CDIAL 13845). Glass, a pot or a bubble \textbf{\hi{फूटता} \hi{है}}; a quarrel can \textbf{\hi{फूट} \hi{पड़ना}}, break out.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{phūṭnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{phūṭnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{patthar lagne se bas kā śīśā phūṭ gayā.} — A stone hit the bus and its glass shattered.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a disturbance, then the Hindi for trouble, then say \emph{phūṭnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{फूटना} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To burst; to shatter\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{लाठी} (lāṭhī)}{लाठी (lāṭhī)}]{\hi{लाठी} (lāṭhī) — a staff; a police baton}

\label{lesson:HI-C316-lathi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for trouble, then the Hindi for to burst.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{लाठी}}
\textbf{\hi{लाठी}} — \emph{lāṭhī} — \textquotedblleft{}a staff; a police baton\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{पुलिस} \hi{ने} \hi{भीड़} \hi{पर} \hi{लाठियाँ} \hi{चलाईं।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pulis ne bhīṛ par lāṭhiyā̃ calāīṁ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police used their batons on the crowd.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{लाठी}} (\emph{lāṭhī}) is inherited from \emph{*laṣṭi}, a stick, a form CDIAL reconstructs (CDIAL 10991). It is the long bamboo staff of a villager or a policeman.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{कर्फ़्यू} (karfyū)}{कर्फ़्यू (karfyū)}]{\hi{कर्फ़्यू} (karfyū) — a curfew}

\label{lesson:HI-C316-karfyu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for to burst, then the Hindi for a staff.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{कर्फ़्यू}}
\textbf{\hi{कर्फ़्यू}} — \emph{karfyū} — \textquotedblleft{}a curfew\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\hi{मेरी} \hi{राय} \hi{में} \hi{कर्फ़्यू} \hi{ज़रूरी} \hi{था।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{merī rāy meṁ karfyū zarūrī thā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In my opinion the curfew was necessary.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{कर्फ़्यू}} (\emph{karfyū}) is borrowed from English \emph{curfew}, taken into Hindi as a masculine noun. A curfew \textbf{\hi{लगता} \hi{है}}, is imposed, and \textbf{\hi{हटता} \hi{है}}, is lifted.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{karfyū}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{merī rāy meṁ karfyū zarūrī thā.} — In my opinion the curfew was necessary.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for to burst, then the Hindi for a staff, then say \emph{karfyū} again
\end{itemize}
